title: The boar who went down
hookLine: the earth has sunk to the bottom, and a boar dives in
carry: avatar means God comes down to where we are
tomorrow: why would a god lift the earth like someone he loves?
last: ONE SIP CAN'T BE TAKEN BACK.

lines: YOU OKAY? FROM THE TOP OF THE STAIRS.
cards: When someone you love has a bad week, it's tempting to call down from the top of the stairs: you okay? The third descent doesn't do that. The earth has sunk to the bottom of the cosmic waters, and nothing can live on her.
Brahma is wondering how to raise her. And then, out of Brahma's own nostril, comes a boar.

teach.b: In the Bhagavata Purana's telling, the boar is tiny at first, the size of a thumb, and in moments grows as large as an elephant, then larger still. That's Varaha, Vishnu's third descent.
He roars, plunges into the waters, and goes all the way down, searching the deep to where the earth lies. He lifts her on his tusks and carries her up.
In the Vishnu Purana, the earth herself speaks as he comes for her, and praises him. Now the big idea, hidden in a word you already know.
Avatar, in Sanskrit avatara, means a descent, a crossing down. That's the teaching: in Hinduism God doesn't only call down from heaven.

teach.h: GOD COMES DOWN TO WHERE WE ARE.
teach.b: God comes down, into the world, in whatever shape the rescue needs. A fish in a flood. A tortoise under a mountain.
And yes, a boar, snout in the mud, because a boar is what digs to the bottom. Many teachers read it this way: no form is too low for God to take, if that's where someone has sunk.

So when Hindus bow to Varaha, they bow to a God who gets wet. This week it might be a friend after bad news, or a brother who won't leave his room. The pattern the story sets isn't advice from the shore.
It's going down to where they are.

how: Varaha is honored as Vishnu's third descent, often shown as a boar-headed figure holding the earth, as a small goddess, on his tusk or arm, and his story is retold from the Vishnu and Bhagavata Puranas.

games.q: at the temple a kid points at Varaha and asks, 'why would God be a pig?' best answer?
o: avatar means coming down; God takes whatever shape can reach the one who's sunk.
boars were royal animals back then, so it was a compliment.
it's only a costume; God never really comes into the world.
games.why: avatara means a descent. Varaha is a boar because a boar digs to the bottom, and that's where the earth was.

practice: Bring to mind one person who seems sunk right now. Silently name what you wish for them; then what makes it hard to reach them; then one plain way to go to where they are, a knock, a walk, a message.
Give each of the three a few slow breaths. If you pray, you might say Om Namo Narayanaya, a prayer to Vishnu many Hindus repeat, with them in mind; if you don't, simply hold them there.
